value.body: A flight instructor teaches student pilots to fly at a flying school. DGCA-approved flying training organisations hire them. A typical day involves ground briefings, instructional flights with students, and debriefs and training records.

items.label: Licence needed
items.value: DGCA CPL plus an instructor rating
items.note: Usually an Assistant Flight Instructor rating first

items.label: DGCA-approved FTOs
items.note: Many run more than one base

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A Commercial Pilot Licence (CPL) from DGCA is the requirement, not a degree. It needs Class 12 with Physics and Maths (these can be added later through NIOS), a DGCA Class 1 medical, passes in the DGCA ground exams (Air Navigation, Meteorology, Air Regulations, Technical) plus a radio telephony licence, and about 200 hours of flying at a DGCA-approved flying school. After the CPL, extra instructor training and a DGCA flight test lead to an instructor rating.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Teaching flying skills step by step
Judging when a student is ready to solo
Staying calm and alert in the cockpit

value.title: At a glance
items: Many pilots instruct to build flying hours before moving to airlines or charter work.
Experienced instructors can become chief flight instructors or examiners.
Work depends on weather and flying school schedules.
Most flying schools are in smaller towns with suitable airfields.
